answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with delayed-settlement escrow: earnings sit in escrow until a fraud-detection horizon passes, and only identities with a clean history withdraw in full. Making a fake is cheap, but like mixing a new pigment for every sonnet, each copy must separately fund its own escrow, wait out the same horizon, and risk forfeiture if challenged. A hundred fakes lock a hundred deposits and wait a hundred delays, while an honest agent pays once, so scale multiplies locked capital and waiting time, not revenue.
